text.en: A Grade 8 student moves to a new city, feels lonely, spends hours on the phone, loses sleep and gets headaches. A doctor advises less screen time and meeting friends. Was he sick, or unhealthy in another way?

Health is more than not falling sick: it includes feeling good physically, staying positive and having strong relationships.
Physical, mental and social well-being together make good health.
Ayurveda teaches that health is a balance of body, mind and surroundings, supported by daily routine and seasonal routine.
Diseases can be infectious, caused by germs like bacteria and viruses, or non-infectious, like diabetes, which do not spread from person to person.
Germs spread through air, water, food, touch and vectors such as mosquitoes, which spread malaria and dengue.
Handwashing, safe drinking water, clean surroundings and vaccination prevent infections.
Vaccines train the immune system, which is why smallpox is gone and polio is nearly gone.
A balanced diet with less oil and sugar, regular exercise and enough sleep help prevent lifestyle diseases such as diabetes.
Too much screen time can cause dry eyes, poor sleep and stress, so we should balance it with play and sleep.
Stress and worry can make us sick, so talking to someone we trust, yoga and rest keep the mind healthy.

why.en: They do not spread from person to person.

text.en: Prevention differs: vector control and hygiene versus diet and exercise.

prompt.en: Is health only about not being sick?

requiredIdeas.en: Health includes physical, mental and social well-being.

points.en: Health = physical, mental and social well-being.
Infectious and non-infectious diseases need different prevention.
Hygiene, vaccines, diet, exercise, sleep and balanced screen time protect health.
